The indented retry paragraph on line 10 then lands in `other`, and `apply_block` appends `other` to the end of the "Stable log prefixes (contractual)" section through `_append_to_section` (lines 301-302) instead of keeping it under the `SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS` bullet.
  WHY: At the next release or sync fold (`mark-stable.yml` / `update_workflows.yml`), the contract text is left as an orphan paragraph after the `LOG_PREFIX.name=` lines. That text covers `outcome=dispatch_retry attempt=<n> dispatch_error=<class>`, `dispatch_attempts=<n>`, the retry budget and env defaults, and the `::warning::` excerpt format. `assemble_agents.py check` does not catch this. Severity disagreement: MAJOR from sonnet, gemini, minimax and glm, NIT from luna; the highest is used.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:1463-1466 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The delta-fallback branch, entered after `single_pass_dispatch_audit "${delta_dispatch_args[@]}"` fails, always logs `outcome=delta_fallback reason=dispatch_rejected`. It does this even when the delta dispatch failed with a transient class (`rate_limited`, `server_error` or `network`) after the shared retry budget ran out, and the comment at lines 1464-1465 still describes only the old-wrapper case.
  WHY: Operators are told that a wrapper rejected the delta inputs when the real cause was a transient outage, for example in `test_delta_fallback_stops_when_the_shared_budget_is_used`. The real class is already in `SINGLE_PASS_DISPATCH_ERROR` but is not logged, which undercuts goal G1. All five reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:322-327 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The final `else echo network` branch in `single_pass_dispatch_error_class` classes any non-empty `gh` error without an HTTP status as `network`, and it is then retried (case at lines 368-370). That includes local errors a retry cannot fix, such as a missing GH_TOKEN, unknown flags or usage errors.
  WHY: A job with a permanent misconfiguration sleeps for up to 40 seconds by default, posts a comment that blames a network error, and then fails, so the operator is sent to the wrong cause. `test_dispatch_error_classes` does not cover usage errors.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1309,4716,4919 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Each of the three hunks adds `SECURITY_PASS_DISPATCH_RETRIES` and `SECURITY_PASS_DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAY_SECS` env rows. No executed `wc -c` and no passing `tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py` confirms the file stays under the 480,000-byte `WORKFLOW_FILE_SIZE_GUARD_BYTES` (tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py:27).
  WHY: If the file reaches 512,000 bytes or more, GitHub silently refuses to start runs and records zero-job "workflow file issue" failures. This is the file most exposed to the limit (incident #4327, tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py:9-10).
